detail.reference: Yes. For example, \(f(z)=1/(1-z^2)\) is holomorphic on the unit disk, since its only poles are at the boundary points \(z=1\) and \(z=-1\). As \(z\) approaches either point from within the disk, \(|f(z)|\to\infty\). More generally, \(\prod_{j=1}^n(z-\zeta_j)^{-1}\) works for any finite collection of distinct boundary points \(\zeta_j\).
